review_scope: static: retail instructions and emitted candidate listing

checks.name: function_identity
checks.rationale: 65 retail bytes, 26 instructions, 1 block, 0 edges; candidate 1/0, score 1.000.

checks.name: cfg_match
checks.rationale: Both decoders and the candidate report 1/0; without the volatile sink -O3 would tail-jump (2 blocks/1 edge), which is why the sink exists.

checks.name: argument_mapping
checks.rationale: Argument1 is read as two dwords: dword 0 becomes the callee's second argument, dword 1 is the base of a 0x24-stride record indexed by argument2 and becomes the callee's first argument; argument3 is pushed first and therefore lands in the ninth slot; the rest forward in order.

checks.name: call_and_return
checks.rationale: One call to the transcribed Texture_UploadMipmapPacket (0x004B23B0) with 0x24 bytes of arguments, returning the callee's value, as retail does.

limitations: The volatile sink is the only non-retail construct; it carries no logic, does not reorder stores and exists only to keep the call/return shape at -O3. It is documented at the site.
The three middle arguments' types stay unestablished; only the forwarded dword values are preserved.
